source_text: Lamina aurea in fronte: Sanctum Domino. Cogitatio in fronte consecrata. Omnis captivitas in obsequium Christi.
thought_title: The golden plate on the forehead
orientation: Origen is interpreting the high priest's vestments, and now explains the golden plate worn on the forehead.
pass_a_gloss: The golden plate on the forehead: Holy to the Lord. The thought on the forehead consecrated. Every captivity into the obedience of Christ.

choices.why: Literal rendering of the physical object worn by the high priest, matching the source's concrete description.
Preserves the inscription's formula as a dedication, keeping the dative of dedication.

choices.english: The thought on the forehead consecrated
choices.why: Keeps the noun phrase structure and the passive participle, showing the thought itself is made holy.
rejected: A consecrated thought on the forehead
The mind consecrated on the forehead

choices.english: Every captivity into the obedience of Christ
choices.why: Preserves the universal 'omnis' and the directional 'in' with accusative, echoing Paul's language of taking every thought captive.
rejected: Every thought made captive to Christ

pass_b_english: The golden plate on the forehead: Holy to the Lord (Exodus 28:36). The thought on the forehead consecrated. Every captivity into the obedience of Christ (2 Corinthians 10:5).

last_rejected.quote: The thought on the forehead consecrated
last_rejected.why: Missing verb; Latin is passive 'is consecrated', not a bare participle.
last_rejected.fix: The thought on the forehead is consecrated.
last_rejected.ruling: Latin 'consecrata' is a participle; 'consecrated' matches it. No finite verb exists in source to be 'missing.'

last_rejected.quote: Every captivity into the obedience of Christ
last_rejected.why: Missing verb; Latin implies 'is led/brings' captivity, not bare noun phrase.
last_rejected.fix: Every captivity into the obedience of Christ (2 Corinthians 10:5).
last_rejected.ruling: Source is a noun phrase with no finite verb; 'into the obedience of Christ' renders 'in obsequium Christi' accurately.
